wga:zearly/1/2mural/3priscil/2velati7.summary: At the centre of the ceiling of the Cubiculum of the Velata, framed by a red circle, a youthful shepherd in a short tunic carries a sheep on his shoulders and stretches out his hand, while a sheep or goat stands on each side and doves perch in the trees above. The gentle, symmetrical composition presides over the chamber's scenes of a Christian woman's life and prayer, placing her under the care of Christ the Good Shepherd.
facts: The chamber takes its name (Velata or Velatio, 'the veiled woman') from the praying, veiled woman painted on its end wall.
The Catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria was used for Christian burials from the late 2nd to the 4th century and was known in antiquity as the 'Queen of the Catacombs'.
wga:zearly/1/2mural/3priscil/2velati7.notes: WGA dates this to 'around 200'; Commons/Wikidata (for the same ceiling) give the second half of the 3rd century (Wikidata 275), which is the more usual dating for the Velata cubiculum. Same ceiling as Q110184746 in this batch, which is marked as a duplicate of this entry.
